docs.title: Porkbun CLI Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to the Porkbun CLI documentation! This powerful command-line tool helps you manage your Porkbun domains and services efficiently.

docs.title: 🌐 Domain Management
docs.text:
• Domain availability checking and suggestions
  • Bulk domain registration and transfer
  • Automated renewal management
  • WHOIS privacy settings
  • Domain price watch functionality
  • Custom nameservers configuration

docs.title: 🔒 DNS Management
docs.text:
• Comprehensive DNS record management
  • Bulk operations and templates
  • DNSSEC configuration and key management
  • Zone file import/export
  • Formatted table output for better readability

docs.title: Step-by-Step Installation
docs.text:
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/ragelink/porkbun-cli.git
cd porkbun-cli

# Set up virtual environment
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate

# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Install in development mode
pip install -e .

docs.title: Docker Installation
docs.text:
# Build the Docker image
docker build -t porkbun-cli .

# Run with volume mount for configuration
docker run -v ~/.porkbun:/root/.porkbun porkbun-cli domains list-all

docs.title: API Access Setup
docs.text:
1. Log in to your Porkbun account
  2. Navigate to "Account" → "API Access"
  3. Create a new API key and save both the API key and Secret key
  4. Enable API access for each domain you want to manage

docs.title: CLI Configuration
docs.text:
# Add a new profile
python -m porkbun.cli config add default --api-key YOUR_API_KEY --secret-key YOUR_SECRET_KEY --make-default

# List profiles
python -m porkbun.cli config list

# Switch profiles
python -m porkbun.cli config use profile_name

docs.title: Domain Management
docs.text:
# Check API connectivity
python -m porkbun.cli account ping

# List all domains
python -m porkbun.cli domains list-all

# Check domain availability with suggestions
python -m porkbun.cli domains check example.com --suggest --compare

# Register a domain
python -m porkbun.cli domains register example.com --years 1

# Add domain to price watch
python -m porkbun.cli domains check example.com --watch 9.99

docs.title: DNS Management
docs.text:
# List DNS records
python -m porkbun.cli dns retrieve example.com

# Create DNS record
python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record example.com A 192.168.1.1 600

# Manage DNSSEC
python -m porkbun.cli dns dnssec enable example.com

docs.title: Portfolio Management
docs.text:
# Tag domains
python -m porkbun.cli account portfolio tag example.com --group clients --tags "important,client1"

# View domain groups
python -m porkbun.cli account portfolio groups

docs.title: Porkbun CLI Command Reference
docs.text: This document provides a comprehensive reference for all available commands in the Porkbun CLI tool.

docs.title: Global Options
docs.text:
These options can be used with any command:

--help          Show help message and exit
--profile TEXT  Specify the profile to use (overrides default)
--verbose       Enable verbose output
--quiet         Suppress all output except errors
--json          Output in JSON format

docs.title: config add
docs.text:
Add a new configuration profile.

python -m porkbun.cli config add PROFILE --api-key KEY --secret-key SECRET [--make-default]

Options: - --api-key TEXT: Your Porkbun API key [required] - --secret-key TEXT: Your Porkbun Secret API key [required] - --make-default: Set this profile as the default

docs.title: config list
docs.text:
List all configured profiles.

python -m porkbun.cli config list

docs.title: config use
docs.text:
Switch to a different profile.

python -m porkbun.cli config use PROFILE

docs.title: config remove
docs.text:

python -m porkbun.cli config remove PROFILE

docs.title: domains register
docs.text:

python -m porkbun.cli domains register DOMAIN [--years INTEGER] [--whois-privacy] [--auto-renew]

docs.title: dns retrieve
docs.text:
Retrieve DNS records for a domain.

docs.title: dns retrieve-records
docs.text:

docs.title: dns create-record
docs.text:
Create a new DNS record.

python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record DOMAIN TYPE CONTENT TTL [--name NAME] [--priority PRIORITY]

Arguments: - DOMAIN: Domain name - TYPE: Record type (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, etc.) - CONTENT: Record content - TTL: Time to live in seconds

Options: - --name NAME: Subdomain name (@ for root) - --priority PRIORITY: Priority (required for MX records)

docs.title: dns update-record
docs.text:
Update an existing DNS record.

python -m porkbun.cli dns update-record DOMAIN RECORD_ID [--type TYPE] [--content CONTENT] [--ttl TTL] [--name NAME] [--priority PRIORITY]

Arguments: - DOMAIN: Domain name - RECORD_ID: ID of the record to update

Options: - Same as dns create-record but all optional

docs.title: dns delete-record
docs.text:
Delete a DNS record.

python -m porkbun.cli dns delete-record DOMAIN RECORD_ID

docs.title: dns batch-update
docs.text:
Create or update multiple DNS records at once using a JSON file.

python -m porkbun.cli dns batch-update DOMAIN BATCH_FILE

Arguments: - DOMAIN: Domain name - BATCH_FILE: Path to JSON file containing DNS records

The JSON file should contain an array of DNS record objects with the following fields: - type: Record type (A, AAAA, MX, CNAME, TXT, etc.) - name: Record name - content: Record content - ttl: Time to live (optional, defaults to 600) - id: Record ID (only needed for updating existing records)

Example JSON file: 

[
    {"type": "A", "name": "test", "content": "192.0.2.1", "ttl": 600},
    {"type": "CNAME", "name": "www", "content": "example.com", "ttl": 600}
]

Note on domain names: When specifying record names, be aware that the Porkbun API may append the domain to the record name. For example, a record name of www might be displayed as www.example.com.example.com in the API response.

docs.title: dns batch-delete
docs.text:
Delete multiple DNS records at once.

python -m porkbun.cli dns batch-delete DOMAIN RECORD_IDS...

Arguments: - DOMAIN: Domain name - RECORD_IDS: One or more record IDs to delete

Example: 

python -m porkbun.cli dns batch-delete example.com 12345 67890 54321

This will delete all the specified records and provide a summary of the operation.

docs.title: dns dnssec status
docs.text:

docs.title: dns dnssec enable
docs.text:

docs.title: dns dnssec disable
docs.text:

docs.title: url list-forwards
docs.text:
List URL forwards for a domain.

python -m porkbun.cli url list-forwards DOMAIN

Arguments: - DOMAIN: Domain name

docs.title: url add-forward
docs.text:
Add URL forward for a domain.

python -m porkbun.cli url add-forward DOMAIN SOURCE DESTINATION [--type TYPE] [--title TITLE]

Arguments: - DOMAIN: Domain name - SOURCE: Source path (e.g., 'blog' or '/' for root) - DESTINATION: Destination URL (e.g., 'https://example.com/blog')

Options: - --type TYPE: Redirect type: 301 (permanent), 302 (temporary), or iframe. Default is 301. - --title TITLE: Title for iframe redirects

docs.title: url delete-forward
docs.text:
Delete URL forward for a domain.

python -m porkbun.cli url delete-forward DOMAIN SOURCE

Arguments: - DOMAIN: Domain name - SOURCE: Source path to delete (e.g., 'blog' or '/' for root)

docs.title: url batch-add
docs.text:
Add multiple URL forwards for a domain using a JSON file.

python -m porkbun.cli url batch-add DOMAIN BATCH_FILE

Arguments: - DOMAIN: Domain name - BATCH_FILE: Path to JSON file containing URL forward definitions

The JSON file should contain an array of forwarding objects with the following fields: - source: Source path (e.g., 'blog' or '/' for root) - destination: Destination URL (e.g., 'https://example.com/blog') - type: Redirect type ('301', '302', or 'iframe') - optional, defaults to '301' - title: Title for iframe redirects - optional

Example JSON file: 

[
    {"source": "blog", "destination": "https://example.com/blog", "type": "301"},
    {"source": "shop", "destination": "https://shop.example.com", "type": "302"}
]

docs.title: email batch-create
docs.text:
Create multiple email forwards for a domain using a JSON file.

python -m porkbun.cli email batch-create DOMAIN BATCH_FILE

Arguments: - DOMAIN: Domain name - BATCH_FILE: Path to JSON file containing email forward definitions

The JSON file should contain an array of forwarding objects with the following fields: - email_prefix: Local part of the email (before @) - forward_to: Email address to forward to

Example JSON file: 

[
    {"email_prefix": "info", "forward_to": "contact@example.com"},
    {"email_prefix": "sales", "forward_to": "sales@example.com"}
]

docs.title: email batch-delete
docs.text:
Delete multiple email forwards at once.

python -m porkbun.cli email batch-delete DOMAIN EMAIL_ID_1 [EMAIL_ID_2 ...]

Arguments: - DOMAIN: Domain name - EMAIL_ID_1 [EMAIL_ID_2 ...]: One or more email forward IDs to delete

docs.title: Domain Setup with Multiple Services
docs.text: This guide explains how to use the Porkbun CLI to set up a domain with multiple service configurations using our helper scripts and templates.

docs.title: Available Tools
docs.text:
The Porkbun CLI provides several tools to simplify domain setup:

  1. Service Templates - Pre-configured DNS records for popular services
  2. Template Customization Tool - Script to personalize templates for your domain
  3. Domain Setup Script - Tool to apply service configurations to your domain

docs.title: Service Templates
docs.text:
Templates for the following services are available:

  • Cloudflare DNS - Basic DNS configuration for Cloudflare
  • Google Workspace - DNS configuration for Google Workspace (formerly G Suite)
  • Microsoft Office 365 - DNS configuration for Microsoft Office 365

Templates are located in the examples/templates/ directory.

docs.title: Using the Setup Script
docs.text: The setup_domain_services.py script automates the process of applying service configurations to your domain.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text: python examples/setup_domain_services.py yourdomain.com --service cloudflare

docs.title: Available Options
docs.text:
• --service - Service to configure (choices: cloudflare, google, microsoft, all)
  • --output-dir - Directory to save configuration files
  • --dry-run - Preview changes without applying them

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Setup with Google Workspace: 

python examples/setup_domain_services.py yourdomain.com --service google

Setup with multiple services: 

python examples/setup_domain_services.py yourdomain.com --service all

Preview changes: 

python examples/setup_domain_services.py yourdomain.com --service microsoft --dry-run

docs.title: Manual Template Customization
docs.text:
If you need to customize templates manually:

  1. Use the customize_template.py script: 

    python examples/customize_template.py examples/templates/office365.json yourdomain.com

  2. Apply the customized template: 

    python -m porkbun.cli workflow setup-domain yourdomain.com --dns-records yourdomain.com_office365.json

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• Always review generated DNS records before applying them to production domains
  • Some services may require additional verification steps not handled by these templates
  • Manual customization may be needed for specific use cases
  • Templates contain placeholder values that will be replaced with your domain name

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
If you encounter issues:

  1. Verify that your Porkbun API credentials are correctly configured
  2. Check that the domain exists in your Porkbun account
  3. Review the generated configuration files for any inconsistencies
  4. Use the --dry-run option to preview changes before applying them

docs.title: Set Up Common DNS Records for a New Domain
docs.text:
Set up standard DNS records for a new website:

# A record for root domain
python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record example.com A 192.168.1.1 600

# CNAME for www subdomain
python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record example.com CNAME example.com 600 --name www

# MX records for email
python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record example.com MX mail.example.com 600 --priority 10
python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record example.com MX mail2.example.com 600 --priority 20

# TXT record for SPF
python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record example.com TXT "v=spf1 include:_spf.example.com ~all" 600

# TXT record for DKIM
python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record example.com TXT "v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=MIGfMA0GCSqGSIb..." 600 --name dkim._domainkey

docs.text:
Configure DNS records for GitHub Pages hosting:

python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record example.com A 185.199.109.153 600
python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record example.com A 185.199.110.153 600
python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record example.com A 185.199.111.153 600

# Create CNAME record for www subdomain
python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record example.com CNAME username.github.io 600 --name www

docs.title: Configure Google Workspace Email
docs.text:
Set up DNS records for Google Workspace (formerly G Suite):

# MX records for Gmail
python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record example.com MX aspmx.l.google.com 3600 --priority 1
python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record example.com MX alt1.aspmx.l.google.com 3600 --priority 5
python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record example.com MX alt2.aspmx.l.google.com 3600 --priority 5
python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record example.com MX alt3.aspmx.l.google.com 3600 --priority 10
python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record example.com MX alt4.aspmx.l.google.com 3600 --priority 10

# SPF record
python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record example.com TXT "v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all" 3600

# DKIM record
python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record example.com TXT "v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=YOUR_DKIM_KEY" 3600 --name google._domainkey

# DMARC record
python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record example.com TXT "v=DMARC1; p=reject; rua=mailto:dmarc@example.com" 3600 --name _dmarc

docs.title: Batch Operations with Shell Scripts
docs.text:
Create a shell script to perform multiple operations:

#!/bin/bash
# setup-domain.sh

# Activate virtual environment
source venv/bin/activate

# Set domain and IP address
DOMAIN=$1
IP_ADDRESS=$2

# Register domain
python -m porkbun.cli domains register $DOMAIN --years 1 --whois-privacy --auto-renew

# Set up DNS records
python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record $DOMAIN A $IP_ADDRESS 600
python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record $DOMAIN CNAME $DOMAIN 600 --name www
python -m porkbun.cli dns create-record $DOMAIN TXT "v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all" 600

# Generate SSL certificate
python -m porkbun.cli ssl generate $DOMAIN --output-dir ./certs/$DOMAIN

echo "Domain $DOMAIN has been set up successfully!"

Combine with jq for advanced filtering of JSON output:

# Find all domains with a specific TLD
python -m porkbun.cli domains list-all --json | jq '.domains[] | select(.tld == "com")'

docs.title: Bulk DNS Updates
docs.text:
Update multiple DNS records at once using a script:

#!/usr/bin/env python
# bulk_dns_update.py

import json
import subprocess
import sys

def update_records(domain, old_ip, new_ip):
    # Get all DNS records
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["python", "-m", "porkbun.cli", "dns", "retrieve-records", domain, "--json"],
        capture_output=True, text=True
    )

    records = json.loads(result.stdout)

    # Filter for A records with the old IP
    for record in records.get("records", []):
        if record["type"] == "A" and record["content"] == old_ip:
            print(f"Updating record {record['id']} from {old_ip} to {new_ip}")

            # Update the record
            subprocess.run([
                "python", "-m", "porkbun.cli", "dns", "update-record",
                domain, record["id"], "--content", new_ip
            ])

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 4:
        print("Usage: ./bulk_dns_update.py DOMAIN OLD_IP NEW_IP")
        sys.exit(1)

    domain = sys.argv[1]
    old_ip = sys.argv[2]
    new_ip = sys.argv[3]

    update_records(domain, old_ip, new_ip)

Usage: 

./bulk_dns_update.py example.com 192.168.1.1 192.168.1.2

docs.title: Service Templates
docs.text: The Porkbun CLI includes ready-to-use templates for setting up domains with popular services such as Cloudflare, Google Workspace, and Microsoft Office 365.

docs.title: Available Templates
docs.text:
The following templates are available in the examples/templates directory:

  • cloudflare_dns.json: Standard DNS records for Cloudflare
  • google_workspace.json: DNS configuration for Google Workspace (formerly G Suite)
  • office365.json: DNS configuration for Microsoft Office 365
  • netlify.json: DNS configuration for Netlify-hosted websites
  • aws_route53.json: DNS configuration for AWS services
  • github_pages.json: DNS configuration for GitHub Pages
  • vercel.json: DNS configuration for Vercel deployments
  • shopify.json: DNS configuration for Shopify e-commerce stores
  • digitalocean.json: DNS configuration for Digital Ocean droplets
  • firebase.json: DNS configuration for Firebase-hosted apps

docs.title: Using the Templates
docs.text:
You can use these templates with the workflow setup-domain command:

python -m porkbun.cli workflow setup-domain example.com --dns-records examples/templates/cloudflare_dns.json

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
1. Customization Required: Some records in these templates need to be customized for your specific domain:
  2. For Office 365: Replace the MX record DOMAIN-com.mail.protection.outlook.com with your domain-specific value (e.g., example-com.mail.protection.outlook.com)

  3. For all templates: Update the DMARC email addresses to use your actual reporting email

  4. A Records: The templates include placeholder A records that point to 192.0.2.1 (a reserved documentation IP). Update these to your actual web server IPs.

  5. Verification Records: These templates don't include domain verification records (e.g., TXT records for Google or Microsoft verification). Add these manually after you initiate the setup with each provider.

docs.title: Template Modification
docs.text:
You can modify these templates for your specific needs:

  1. Create a copy of a template: 

    cp examples/templates/google_workspace.json myconfig.json

  2. Edit the file with your customizations: 

    nano myconfig.json

  3. Apply the customized template: 

    python -m porkbun.cli workflow setup-domain example.com --dns-records myconfig.json

docs.title: Batch Setup
docs.text:
You can set up a domain with multiple services at once using a batch file. The examples/services_setup.yaml file demonstrates this:

python -m porkbun.cli batch run examples/services_setup.yaml

Before running this batch file, make a copy and replace DOMAIN with your actual domain name:

sed 's/DOMAIN/example.com/g' examples/services_setup.yaml > my_setup.yaml
python -m porkbun.cli batch run my_setup.yaml

docs.title: Custom Service Templates
docs.text:
Creating your own service template is straightforward:

  1. Create a JSON file with the required DNS records
  2. Include all required record types (A, CNAME, MX, TXT, etc.)
  3. Follow the format: 
    [
  {
    "type": "RECORD_TYPE",
    "name": "SUBDOMAIN",
    "content": "VALUE",
    "ttl": TTL_VALUE
  },
  ...
]

For services that require specific email forwards or URL forwards, create separate template files for these configurations and apply them with the appropriate commands.

docs.title: Netlify
docs.text:
The Netlify template includes DNS records for hosting a website on Netlify:

  • A Record: Points to Netlify's load balancer IP
  • CNAME Records: For www, blog, and app subdomains, pointing to your Netlify app
  • SPF Record: Includes Netlify and Mailgun mail servers
  • DMARC Record: Basic DMARC policy
  • MX Records: Configured for Mailgun email handling
  • ACME Challenge CNAME: For Netlify's SSL certificate management

docs.title: Custom Values to Replace:
docs.text:

  • _netlify-site-verification: Update with your Netlify verification code

To apply with automatic customization:

python examples/setup_domain_services.py example.com --service netlify

docs.text:

  • S3 Website Hosting: CNAME record for www subdomain
  • API Gateway: CNAME record for api subdomain

  • SES (Simple Email Service): MX and verification records

docs.title: Setting Up Porkbun CLI
docs.text: This guide provides detailed instructions for setting up and configuring the Porkbun CLI tool.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.8 or higher
  • pip (Python package manager)
  • Git (for cloning the repository)
  • Porkbun account with API access enabled

docs.title: Method 1: Using Virtual Environment (Recommended)
docs.text:
This method isolates the Porkbun CLI dependencies from your system Python packages.

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/ragelink/porkbun-cli.git
cd porkbun-cli

# Create and activate a virtual environment
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate

# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Install in development mode
pip install -e .

To deactivate the virtual environment when you're done:

deactivate

docs.title: Method 2: Docker Installation
docs.text:
Using Docker avoids installing Python and dependencies directly on your system.

# Clone the repository (if you haven't already)
git clone https://github.com/ragelink/porkbun-cli.git
cd porkbun-cli

# Build the Docker image
docker build -t porkbun-cli .

# Run a command using the Docker container
docker run -v ~/.porkbun:/root/.porkbun porkbun-cli config list

The volume mount (-v ~/.porkbun:/root/.porkbun) ensures your configuration persists between container runs.

docs.title: API Access Setup
docs.text:
Before using the CLI, you need to obtain API credentials from Porkbun:

  1. Log in to your Porkbun account at https://porkbun.com/account/login
  2. Navigate to "Account" → "API Access"
  3. Click "Create API Key"
  4. Save both the API key and Secret key securely
  5. For each domain you want to manage:
  6. Go to the domain management page
  7. Enable "API Access" for that domain
  8. This step is crucial; the API won't work for domains without this enabled

docs.title: CLI Configuration
docs.text: The CLI supports multiple profiles, allowing you to manage different API keys (e.g., for different Porkbun accounts).

docs.title: Adding a Profile
docs.text:
# Activate your virtual environment if using Method 1
source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate

# Add a new profile (default)
python -m porkbun.cli config add default --api-key YOUR_API_KEY --secret-key YOUR_SECRET_KEY --make-default

# Add additional profiles (optional)
python -m porkbun.cli config add work --api-key WORK_API_KEY --secret-key WORK_SECRET_KEY

docs.title: Managing Profiles
docs.text:
# List all configured profiles
python -m porkbun.cli config list

# Switch to a different profile
python -m porkbun.cli config use work

# Remove a profile
python -m porkbun.cli config remove profile_name

docs.title: Verifying Installation
docs.text:
To verify that the CLI is properly installed and configured:

# Test API connectivity
python -m porkbun.cli account ping

# If configured correctly, you should see a success message with your IP address

docs.text: For convenience, you can set up a shell alias to avoid typing the full command:

docs.title: Bash/Zsh
docs.text:
Add to your ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc:

alias porkbun='python -m porkbun.cli'

Then reload your shell:

source ~/.bashrc  # or source ~/.zshrc

Now you can use shortened commands:

porkbun domains list-all

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
To update to the latest version:

# Navigate to your porkbun-cli directory
cd /path/to/porkbun-cli

# Pull the latest changes
git pull

# Activate your virtual environment (if using Method 1)
source venv/bin/activate

# Update dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Reinstall in development mode (if needed)
pip install -e .

docs.text:
1. Python Version Error:
  2. Error: Python 3.8 or higher is required

  3. Solution: Install a newer version of Python

  5. Error: Package 'X' conflicts with 'Y'

docs.title: DNS Async Operation Fix
docs.text:
The DNS retrieve command currently has an issue with asynchronous operations not being properly awaited. To fix:

  1. Open porkbun/commands/dns.py
  2. Focus on the retrieve and retrieve_records functions
  3. Import the asyncio module at the top of the file
  4. Wrap the make_request calls with asyncio.run() to properly handle the coroutines
  5. This should fix the "coroutine was never awaited" warning

docs.title: Domain API Access Error Handling
docs.text:
When a domain is not opted in to API access, the error message is not very helpful. To improve:

  1. Add try/except blocks in the DNS functions to catch the specific 400 error
  2. When catching the "Domain is not opted in to API access" error, provide a clear message
  3. Include instructions on how to enable API access in the Porkbun dashboard
  4. Consider adding a check_domain_api_access helper function in the API module

docs.title: Testing Strategy
docs.text:
1. Test the DNS retrieve command with ragelink.com first (has API access issue)
  2. Test with a domain that has API access enabled
  3. Verify both the async fix and the improved error messages

docs.title: Code Improvement Opportunities
docs.text:
1. Look for other async functions in the codebase that might have similar issues
  2. Enhance table formatting for DNS record output
  3. Add colorized output for error messages
  4. Consider adding batch operations for DNS records

docs.title: Porkbun CLI Troubleshooting Guide
docs.text: This guide helps you diagnose and solve common issues when using the Porkbun CLI.

docs.title: Problem: Authentication Failed
docs.text:
Error message: Authentication failed, Invalid API key, or Invalid credentials

Possible causes: - Incorrect API key or Secret key - Expired API key - API access disabled in Porkbun account

Solutions: 1. Verify your API key and Secret key are correct: 

python -m porkbun.cli config list
2. Create a new API key in your Porkbun account and update the CLI: 
python -m porkbun.cli config add default --api-key NEW_KEY --secret-key NEW_SECRET --make-default
3. Check API access is enabled in your Porkbun account dashboard.

docs.title: Problem: Domain Not Authorized
docs.text:
Error message: Domain is not opted in to API access or Not authorized for domain

Possible causes: - API access not enabled for the specific domain - Domain not owned by your Porkbun account

Solutions: 1. Log in to your Porkbun account 2. Navigate to the domain management page for the specific domain 3. Find the "API Access" option and enable it 4. Try your command again

docs.title: Problem: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
Error message: Too many requests or Rate limit exceeded

Possible causes: - Sending too many API requests in a short period - Running multiple commands simultaneously

Solutions: 1. Wait a few minutes before trying again 2. Add delays between API calls in scripts 3. Check your code for unnecessary API calls in loops

docs.title: Problem: DNS Record Not Creating
docs.text:
Error message: Error creating record or Invalid record data

Possible causes: - Invalid DNS record format - Incorrect record type - Duplicate record

Solutions: 1. Check the format of your record data 2. Verify the record type is supported (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, etc.) 3. List existing records to check for duplicates: 

python -m porkbun.cli dns retrieve example.com

docs.title: Problem: Async Operation Warning
docs.text:
Error message: Coroutine was never awaited or similar warning

Possible causes: - Bug in the DNS retrieval function

Solutions: 1. Update to the latest version of the CLI 2. Try using the --json flag which may bypass this issue: 

python -m porkbun.cli dns retrieve example.com --json
3. As a temporary workaround, use a direct API call: 
curl -X POST "https://porkbun.com/api/json/v3/dns/retrieve/{DOMAIN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"apikey":"YOUR_API_KEY","secretapikey":"YOUR_SECRET_KEY"}'

docs.title: Problem: Command Not Found
docs.text:
Error message: Command not found, ModuleNotFoundError, or similar

Possible causes: - Virtual environment not activated - Package not installed correctly - PATH not configured correctly

Solutions: 1. Ensure your virtual environment is activated: 

source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
2. Reinstall the package: 
pip install -e .
3. Verify the installation location is in your PATH

docs.title: Problem: Missing Dependencies
docs.text:
Error message: ImportError: No module named X

Possible causes: - Missing Python package - Incorrect Python version

Solutions: 1. Install required dependencies: 

pip install -r requirements.txt
2. Check your Python version: 
python --version  # Should be 3.8 or higher

docs.title: Problem: Configuration Not Found
docs.text:
Error message: No configuration found or No profile configured

Possible causes: - Configuration file missing or corrupted - No default profile set

Solutions: 1. Add a new configuration profile: 

python -m porkbun.cli config add default --api-key YOUR_API_KEY --secret-key YOUR_SECRET_KEY --make-default
2. Check if configuration exists: 
python -m porkbun.cli config list
3. Check the configuration file location: - Linux/macOS: ~/.porkbun/config.json - Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.porkbun\config.json

docs.title: Problem: Configuration Persistence
docs.text:
Error message: No configuration found when running in Docker

Possible causes: - Volume mount not set up correctly - Permissions issue

Solutions: 1. Use the volume mount to persist configuration: 

docker run -v ~/.porkbun:/root/.porkbun porkbun-cli config list
2. Create the configuration directory first: 
mkdir -p ~/.porkbun
3. Check file permissions on the host directory

docs.title: Problem: Docker Command Output
docs.text:
Error message: Garbled or incomplete output from Docker

Possible causes: - Terminal size issues - TTY allocation

Solutions: 1. Add TTY allocation to the Docker command: 

docker run -it -v ~/.porkbun:/root/.porkbun porkbun-cli domains list-all
2. Use the --json flag for structured output: 
docker run -v ~/.porkbun:/root/.porkbun porkbun-cli domains list-all --json

docs.title: Enable Verbose Output
docs.text:
Add the --verbose flag to see detailed information about what's happening:

python -m porkbun.cli domains list-all --verbose

docs.title: Check API Response
docs.text:
Use the --json flag to see the raw API response:

python -m porkbun.cli account ping --json

docs.title: Inspect Configuration
docs.text:
Check your current configuration:

python -m porkbun.cli config list

docs.title: Check Logs
docs.text: Logs are stored in: - Linux/macOS: ~/.porkbun/logs/ - Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.porkbun\logs\

docs.title: Test Network Connectivity
docs.text:
Test if you can reach the Porkbun API server:

curl -I https://porkbun.com/api/json/v3/ping

docs.title: Getting More Help
docs.text:
If you're still experiencing issues:

  1. Check the GitHub Issues to see if your problem has been reported
  2. Open a new issue with:
  3. Command you're trying to run
  4. Error message (full traceback if available)
  5. Your operating system and Python version
  6. Steps to reproduce

docs.title: Workflow Commands
docs.text: The workflow module provides commands for chaining multiple operations together, allowing you to automate common tasks and set up domains more efficiently.

docs.title: Setup Domain
docs.text:
The setup-domain command allows you to configure multiple aspects of a domain in a single operation, including DNS records, email forwards, and URL forwards.

python -m porkbun.cli workflow setup-domain DOMAIN [OPTIONS]

Arguments: - DOMAIN: The domain to configure

Options: - --dns-records PATH: Path to a JSON file containing DNS records - --email-forwards PATH: Path to a JSON file containing email forwards - --url-forwards PATH: Path to a JSON file containing URL forwards - --sequential/--parallel: Run tasks sequentially or in parallel (default: sequential)

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Set up a new domain with DNS records, email forwards, and URL forwards:

python -m porkbun.cli workflow setup-domain example.com \
    --dns-records dns.json \
    --email-forwards email_forwards.json \
    --url-forwards url_forwards.json

docs.title: Configuration Files
docs.text: Each configuration file should follow the format expected by the corresponding batch command:

docs.title: Export Configuration
docs.text:
The export-config command exports the current configuration of a domain to JSON files that can be used with the setup-domain command or individually with other commands.

python -m porkbun.cli workflow export-config DOMAIN [OPTIONS]

Arguments: - DOMAIN: The domain to export configuration from

Options: - --dns-types TYPE...: DNS record types to include (e.g., A, AAAA, CNAME) - --include-email/--exclude-email: Include or exclude email forwards (default: include) - --include-url/--exclude-url: Include or exclude URL forwards (default: include) - --output-dir PATH: Directory to save configuration files (default: current directory)

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Export all configuration for a domain:

python -m porkbun.cli workflow export-config example.com --output-dir ./configs

Export only specific DNS record types:

python -m porkbun.cli workflow export-config example.com --dns-types A CNAME MX --exclude-email --exclude-url

docs.title: Migrating Domains
docs.text: When moving a domain from one provider to Porkbun, you can export the configuration from the old provider, convert it to the Porkbun format, and then use setup-domain to apply it all at once.

docs.title: Creating Development Environments
docs.text:
Create separate configuration files for development, staging, and production environments, then apply them as needed:

# Set up development environment
python -m porkbun.cli workflow setup-domain dev.example.com --dns-records dev_dns.json --email-forwards dev_email.json

# Set up production environment
python -m porkbun.cli workflow setup-domain example.com --dns-records prod_dns.json --email-forwards prod_email.json

docs.title: Creating Domain Templates
docs.text:
Create template configuration files for common domain setups (e.g., business websites, blogs, e-commerce sites) and apply them to new domains:

python -m porkbun.cli workflow setup-domain new-business.com --dns-records templates/business_dns.json --email-forwards templates/business_email.json

docs.title: Tips and Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Test Configuration Files: Before running setup-domain on a production domain, validate your configuration files to ensure they contain the correct settings.

  2. Use Version Control: Keep your domain configuration files in version control to track changes and easily roll back if needed.

  3. Backup Before Changes: Always export the current configuration before making major changes to a domain.

  4. Use Sequential Mode for Complex Setups: For complex domain setups or when the order of operations matters, use the sequential mode to ensure operations are completed in order.

  5. Organize Configuration Files: Use a consistent naming scheme and directory structure for your configuration files to easily find what you need.

docs.title: Service Templates
docs.text: To simplify common domain setups, the Porkbun CLI provides pre-configured DNS templates for popular services. These templates can be used with the setup-domain command to quickly configure a domain for use with these services.

docs.title: Available Service Templates
docs.text:
The following service templates are available in the examples/templates/ directory:

  • cloudflare_dns.json - DNS configuration for Cloudflare
  • google_workspace.json - DNS configuration for Google Workspace (formerly G Suite)
  • office365.json - DNS configuration for Microsoft Office 365
  • netlify.json - DNS configuration for Netlify-hosted websites
  • aws_route53.json - DNS configuration for AWS services
  • github_pages.json - DNS configuration for GitHub Pages
  • vercel.json - DNS configuration for Vercel deployments
  • shopify.json - DNS configuration for Shopify e-commerce stores
  • digitalocean.json - DNS configuration for Digital Ocean droplets
  • firebase.json - DNS configuration for Firebase-hosted apps

docs.title: Using Service Templates
docs.text:
You can use these templates directly with the setup-domain command:

python -m porkbun.cli workflow setup-domain example.com --dns-records examples/templates/office365.json

However, these templates contain placeholder values that need to be customized for your domain. The CLI provides a helper script to simplify this process.

docs.title: Helper Script for Service Templates
docs.text:
The setup_domain_services.py script automates the process of customizing and applying service templates:

python examples/setup_domain_services.py example.com --service microsoft

This will: 1. Customize the service template for your domain 2. Save the customized template to a file 3. Apply the template to your domain using the setup-domain command

docs.title: Available Options
docs.text:
• --service: Service to configure (choices: cloudflare, google, microsoft, all)
  • --output-dir: Directory to save configuration files
  • --dry-run: Preview changes without applying them

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Set up a domain with Google Workspace
python examples/setup_domain_services.py example.com --service google

# Preview changes for Microsoft Office 365
python examples/setup_domain_services.py example.com --service microsoft --dry-run

# Set up a domain with all service templates
python examples/setup_domain_services.py example.com --service all

For more detailed information on using service templates, see the Domain Setup Guide.

docs.title: Commands Reference
docs.text: This document provides a complete reference of all available commands in the Porkbun CLI.

docs.title: account ping
docs.text:
Check the API connection status.

porkbun account ping

docs.title: account info
docs.text:
Retrieve account information.

porkbun account info

docs.title: account pricing
docs.text:
Get pricing information for domains.

porkbun account pricing

docs.title: config add
docs.text:
Add a new profile with API credentials.

porkbun config add PROFILE_NAME --api-key YOUR_API_KEY --secret-key YOUR_SECRET_KEY [--make-default]

docs.title: config list
docs.text:
List all configured profiles.

porkbun config list

docs.title: config use
docs.text:
Switch to a different profile.

porkbun config use PROFILE_NAME

docs.title: config delete
docs.text:
Delete a profile.

porkbun config delete PROFILE_NAME

docs.title: domains list-all
docs.text:
List all domains in your account.

porkbun domains list-all [--output table|json|csv]

docs.title: domains check
docs.text:
Check domain availability.

porkbun domains check DOMAIN [--tlds TLD1,TLD2,TLD3] [--suggest] [--compare]

docs.title: domains register
docs.text:
Register a new domain.

porkbun domains register DOMAIN [--years YEARS] [--whois-privacy ENABLED|DISABLED]

docs.title: domains renew
docs.text:
Renew a domain.

porkbun domains renew DOMAIN [--years YEARS]

docs.title: domains transfer
docs.text:
Transfer a domain to Porkbun.

porkbun domains transfer DOMAIN --auth-code AUTH_CODE [--years YEARS]

docs.title: dns retrieve
docs.text:
List all DNS records for a domain.

porkbun dns retrieve DOMAIN [--output table|json|csv]

docs.title: dns create-record
docs.text:
Create a new DNS record.

porkbun dns create-record DOMAIN TYPE CONTENT TTL [--name NAME] [--priority PRIORITY]

Example: 

porkbun dns create-record example.com A 192.168.1.1 600 --name www

docs.title: dns edit-record
docs.text:
Edit an existing DNS record.

porkbun dns edit-record DOMAIN RECORD_ID --content CONTENT [--ttl TTL] [--name NAME] [--priority PRIORITY]

docs.title: dns delete-record
docs.text:
Delete a DNS record.

porkbun dns delete-record DOMAIN RECORD_ID

docs.title: dns dnssec
docs.text:
Manage DNSSEC for a domain.

porkbun dns dnssec enable|disable|status DOMAIN

docs.title: ssl retrieve
docs.text:
Get SSL certificate information.

porkbun ssl retrieve DOMAIN

docs.title: ssl create
docs.text:
Create a new SSL certificate.

porkbun ssl create DOMAIN

docs.title: url list
docs.text:
List URL forwards for a domain.

porkbun url list DOMAIN

docs.title: url add
docs.text:
Add a URL forward.

porkbun url add DOMAIN FROM_PATH TO_URL [--type 301|302|cloaked]

docs.title: url delete
docs.text:
Delete a URL forward.

porkbun url delete DOMAIN FORWARD_ID

docs.title: url batch-add
docs.text:
Add multiple URL forwards from a JSON file.

porkbun url batch-add DOMAIN --file FORWARDS_FILE.json

docs.title: email list
docs.text:
List email forwards for a domain.

porkbun email list DOMAIN

docs.title: email add
docs.text:
Add an email forward.

porkbun email add DOMAIN LOCAL_PART TO_EMAIL

Example: 

porkbun email add example.com info info@another-domain.com

docs.title: email update
docs.text:
Update an email forward.

porkbun email update DOMAIN FORWARD_ID --to TO_EMAIL

docs.title: email delete
docs.text:
Delete an email forward.

porkbun email delete DOMAIN FORWARD_ID

docs.title: workflow list
docs.text:
List available workflows.

porkbun workflow list

docs.title: workflow setup-domain
docs.text:
Set up a domain with predefined services.

porkbun workflow setup-domain DOMAIN [--service SERVICE] [--template TEMPLATE_FILE]

Available services: - cloudflare - google - office365 - netlify - aws - github - vercel - shopify - digitalocean - firebase - all

docs.title: batch run
docs.text:
Run a batch file with multiple commands.

porkbun batch run BATCH_FILE.yaml [--dry-run]

docs.title: monitor list
docs.text:
List monitored domains.

porkbun monitor list

docs.title: monitor add
docs.text:
Add a domain to monitoring.

porkbun monitor add DOMAIN [--check-interval MINUTES] [--notification-email EMAIL]

docs.title: monitor remove
docs.text:
Remove a domain from monitoring.

porkbun monitor remove DOMAIN

docs.title: Formatting Options
docs.text:
Most commands support the following output formats:

  • --output table (default): Format output as a table
  • --output json: Format output as JSON
  • --output csv: Format output as CSV

docs.title: Email Forwarding Cheat Sheet
docs.text: This cheat sheet provides quick examples for common email forwarding tasks using the Porkbun CLI.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Porkbun account with API access
  • Domain registered with Porkbun
  • API access enabled for your domain
  • Porkbun CLI installed and configured

docs.title: List all email forwards for a domain
docs.text: python -m porkbun.cli email list-forwards example.com

docs.title: Create a single email forward
docs.text:
Create a forward from info@example.com to contact@example.com:

python -m porkbun.cli email create-forward example.com info contact@example.com

docs.title: Update an existing email forward
docs.text:
Update the destination of a forward with ID 12345:

python -m porkbun.cli email update-forward example.com 12345 new-email@example.com

docs.title: Delete an email forward
docs.text:
Delete a forward with ID 12345:

python -m porkbun.cli email delete-forward example.com 12345

docs.title: Create multiple email forwards using JSON
docs.text:
First, create a JSON file with your email forwards:

[
  {
    "email_prefix": "info",
    "forward_to": "contact@example.com"
  },
  {
    "email_prefix": "sales",
    "forward_to": "sales@example.com"
  },
  {
    "email_prefix": "support",
    "forward_to": "help@example.com"
  }
]

Then run the batch creation command:

python -m porkbun.cli email batch-create example.com email_forwards.json

docs.text: python -m porkbun.cli email batch-delete example.com 12345 67890 54321

python -m porkbun.cli email batch-create example.com business_forwards.json

docs.title: Tips and Tricks
docs.text:
1. Finding Forward IDs: Use the list-forwards command to get the IDs needed for updating or deleting forwards.

  2. Organizing JSON Files: Create separate JSON files for different types of forwards (roles, departments, individuals) to keep things organized.

  3. Backup Before Deleting: Always list and save your current forwards before making batch deletions.

  4. Validation: The CLI validates email formats, but you can use the --help flag to understand all requirements.

  5. Error Handling: The CLI provides detailed error messages if something goes wrong with API access or if the domain is not properly configured.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
If you encounter any issues:

  1. API Access: Ensure your domain has API access enabled in the Porkbun dashboard.

  2. Authentication: Check that your API keys are correctly configured.

  3. Rate Limiting: If you receive rate limit errors, space out your requests.

  4. Invalid Domain: Make sure the domain is registered with Porkbun and spelled correctly.

  5. Email Format: Ensure all email addresses follow standard format (user@domain.tld).

For more details on any command, use the --help flag:

python -m porkbun.cli email list-forwards --help

docs.title: Testing Guide
docs.text: This guide explains the testing approach for the Porkbun CLI project and how to write and run tests.

docs.title: Testing Framework
docs.text:
We use pytest for testing. The test suite is organized as follows:

  • tests/unit/: Unit tests for individual components
  • tests/integration/: Integration tests that interact with the Porkbun API

docs.title: All Tests
docs.text: pytest

docs.title: Unit Tests Only
docs.text: pytest tests/unit/

docs.title: Test Coverage
docs.text:
To generate a test coverage report:

pytest --cov=porkbun tests/

For a detailed HTML coverage report:

pytest --cov=porkbun --cov-report=html tests/

docs.title: Unit Tests
docs.text:
Unit tests should be isolated and not make actual API calls. Use mocking to simulate API responses:

import pytest
from unittest.mock import patch, MagicMock

from porkbun.commands.domains import check_domain

@patch('porkbun.commands.domains.make_request')
def test_check_domain(mock_make_request):
    # Set up mock response
    mock_response = {
        "status": "SUCCESS",
        "available": True,
        "tld": "com",
        "domain": "example.com",
        "price": 9.98
    }
    mock_make_request.return_value = mock_response

    # Call the function
    result = check_domain("example.com")

    # Assert the result
    assert result["available"] is True
    assert result["domain"] == "example.com"

    # Verify the mock was called correctly
    mock_make_request.assert_called_once_with(
        endpoint="check",
        method="post",
        data={"domain": "example.com"}
    )

docs.title: Integration Tests
docs.text:
Integration tests make actual API calls and should be skipped by default to prevent accidental charges:

import pytest
import os
from porkbun.commands.domains import check_domain

@pytest.mark.skipif(
    "PORKBUN_RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS" not in os.environ,
    reason="Integration tests are disabled. Set PORKBUN_RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 to run."
)
def test_check_domain_integration():
    result = check_domain("example1234567890.com")
    assert "available" in result
    assert "domain" in result

To run integration tests:

PORKBUN_RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 pytest tests/integration/

docs.title: Test Fixtures
docs.text:
We use pytest fixtures for common setup tasks:

import pytest
import json
from pathlib import Path

docs.title: Installation Guide
docs.text: This guide explains how to install the Porkbun CLI on your system.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.8 or higher
  • pip (Python package installer)
  • Porkbun account with API access

docs.title: From PyPI (Recommended)
docs.text:
The easiest way to install the Porkbun CLI is from PyPI:

pip install porkbun-cli

To install in a virtual environment (recommended):

python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
pip install porkbun-cli

docs.title: From Source
docs.text:
To install from source:

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/ragelink/porkbun-cli.git
cd porkbun-cli

# Set up virtual environment
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate

# Install dependencies and package
pip install -e .

docs.title: Docker Installation
docs.text:
For Docker users:

# Build the Docker image
docker build -t porkbun-cli .

# Run with volume mount for configuration
docker run -v ~/.porkbun:/root/.porkbun porkbun-cli --help

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
To verify that the installation was successful:

porkbun --version

or

python -m porkbun.cli --version

docs.title: Setting Up API Access
docs.text:
Before using the CLI, you'll need to set up your Porkbun API credentials:

  1. Log in to your Porkbun account
  2. Navigate to "Account" → "API Access"
  3. Create a new API key and save both the API key and Secret key
  4. Enable API access for each domain you want to manage

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
Configure the CLI with your API credentials:

porkbun config add default --api-key YOUR_API_KEY --secret-key YOUR_SECRET_KEY --make-default

or

python -m porkbun.cli config add default --api-key YOUR_API_KEY --secret-key YOUR_SECRET_KEY --make-default

docs.title: Test the Connection
docs.text:
Test your API connection:

porkbun account ping

If successful, you'll see a success message confirming your API connection works.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
To upgrade to the latest version:

pip install --upgrade porkbun-cli

docs.title: Common Installation Issues
docs.text:
1. Python Version Error

If you receive an error about Python version requirements, make sure you have Python 3.8 or higher installed:

python --version
  1. Permission Denied

If you encounter permission issues during installation, try using:

pip install --user porkbun-cli
  1. Package Not Found

If the porkbun command is not found after installation, ensure that your Python scripts directory is in your PATH.

docs.text: If you encounter any issues, check the Troubleshooting Guide or create an issue on the GitHub repository.

docs.title: Quick Start Guide
docs.text: This guide will help you get started with the Porkbun CLI quickly.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install the Porkbun CLI:

pip install porkbun-cli

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Set up your API credentials:

porkbun config add default --api-key YOUR_API_KEY --secret-key YOUR_SECRET_KEY --make-default

docs.title: Check Connection
docs.text:
Test your API connection:

porkbun account ping

docs.title: List Your Domains
docs.text:
View all domains in your account:

porkbun domains list-all

docs.title: Check Domain Availability
docs.text:
Check if a domain is available for registration:

porkbun domains check example.com

Check multiple TLDs for a domain name:

porkbun domains check example --tlds com,net,org,io

docs.title: DNS Management
docs.text:
List DNS records for a domain:

porkbun dns retrieve example.com

Create a new DNS record:

porkbun dns create-record example.com A 192.168.1.1 600

docs.title: Service Templates
docs.text:
Set up a domain with a service (e.g., Google Workspace):

porkbun workflow setup-domain example.com --service google

docs.title: Batch Operations
docs.text:
Batch update multiple DNS records:

porkbun batch run examples/dns_updates.yaml

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text:
Run a predefined workflow:

porkbun workflow setup-domain example.com

docs.title: Getting Help
docs.text:
Display all available commands:

porkbun --help

Get help on a specific command:

porkbun domains --help
